To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the G-protein beta-subunit (GNB 3) C825T polymorphism is associated with type II diabetes in the United Arab Emirates.
the GNB 3 T825 allele is significantly associated with type II diabetes mellitis.
GNB3 82T allele is positively associated with type 2 diabetes mellitus in an Emirati population.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the genetic basis of NIDDM and the role of GNB3 gene in its pathogenesis.
the identification of genetic markers of type 2 DM in a population that has a high prevalence of the disease.
the identification of genetic factors that may influence susceptibility to type II diabetes in Emiratis and may help in the development of a genetic test for type II diabetes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the GNB-3 gene may be involved in DM through pathways that are different from the ones implicated in obesity.
the GNB 825 T allele may be a genetic marker for NIDDM in Emirati.
the T825 allele of GNB3 gene is a risk factor for type 2 DM.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the GNB 825 allele is associated with type II diabetes mellitis and may be a useful marker for the prediction of type II diabetes mellitits in the UAE population.
the T825 allele is a risk factor in the development of DM.
the G-protein beta3 subunit (T825 allele) may be a genetic marker for type 2 DM in the United Arab Emirates population.

GNB3 826 T/T genotype could be a marker of NIDDM risk.
the T825 variant of the GNB3 gene is significantly associated with the development of type II diabetes.
